A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ALMC posterior-sampling work. Their text, equations, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison across the reorganization.

before.justification: v1 contains theoretical results, analytic examples, and explanatory schematics, but no original experimental or simulation outcomes, including in Appendices A–E.

after.justification: Figure 4 and Remark 4.7 report ALMC sampling outcomes for a synthetic two-dimensional prior, displaying estimated sample densities and describing recovered modes.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same Gaussian initialization, likelihood-based LMC warm start, and slowed annealed Langevin updates. The revised explanations and parameter guidance do not introduce a new algorithmic component.

E1.justification: v2 adds an actual synthetic sampling scenario with a two-dimensional vertical-bar prior, two gaps, and a noisy vertical-coordinate measurement. Related bars in v1 illustrate theoretical arguments rather than evaluated sampling outcomes.

E2.justification: Neither version empirically evaluates competing sampling methods. v2 discusses ordinary LMC theoretically, but its new sampling illustration reports only ALMC.

E3.justification: The new experiment evaluates ALMC qualitatively through sampled-density plots and coordinate marginals, using a vertical measurement of -0.25. This introduces an evaluation procedure rather than revising an existing experiment.

E4.justification: Figure 4 and Remark 4.7 add a case study examining whether ALMC discovers separated modes and reduces mass on bars whose gaps conflict with the measurement. v1 provides conceptual illustrations without this sampling evidence.

E5.justification: v2 introduces kernel density estimation of ALMC samples in Figure 4, adding a statistical estimation procedure absent from v1. Neither version reports seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: v2 newly reports that the sampler discovers every illustrated mode and assigns smaller weights to the two gapped modes. There are no corresponding empirical results in v1, so this is added qualitative evidence rather than a measured performance improvement.

T1.justification: v2 removes Proposition 3.1 and Appendix D's LSI-tilting counterexamples, replaces v1's one-dimensional mixture example with two-dimensional mixture derivations, and adds the local conditional-KL lemma and proofs in Lemmas D.1–D.3. It also changes the likelihood Hessian assumption from a lower to an upper bound, revises Lemma C.1 accordingly, changes Lemma A.4's equality to an inequality, and removes the supremum in Lemma C.7. The main polynomial convergence guarantees remain.

C1.justification: The central simultaneous KL-to-noised-posterior and FI-to-true-posterior claim is retained. However, v2's introduction explicitly claims avoidance of mode collapse in the Gaussian-mixture setting, strengthening v1's statement that the combined guarantee potentially avoids this failure.

C2.justification: v2 refines the existing local-versus-global interpretation through conditional KL closeness on small balls and an explicit mode-weight discussion relative to the noised-prior posterior. Section 4.1 and Remark 4.7 further explain how this distinction relates to mode collapse and the new sampling illustration.

D1.justification: The method discussion changes the documented starting-noise scale from T_ws proportional to log(1/epsilon) to epsilon^-2 log(1/epsilon), while Lemma 4.3 retains logarithmic guidance. This is a change in documented parameter guidance; the PDFs do not establish changed implementation settings. v2 supplies no concrete run parameters or sample counts for its new illustration.

R1.justification: v2 adds Geman and Hwang (1986) when distinguishing temperature annealing from Gaussian annealing in Remark 2.2. The broader positioning against posterior-sampling hardness and existing sampling approaches remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 substantially rewrites the contributions and explanatory narrative, incorporates the former standalone hardness section into Background, and develops a dedicated local/global-guarantees subsection. It also reorganizes the concluding appendices, expands notation explanations, and changes citation style throughout.

P2.justification: v2 removes the LSI illustrations formerly shown in Figures 2 and 6 and adds the sampled-density Figure 4. Other diagrams are retained across renumbering, Algorithm 1 is relocated, and the single-column layout becomes denser; no tables are introduced.

improvement.justification: v2 offers clearer explanatory structure, a useful sampling illustration, and several mathematical corrections. However, its new Lemma D.1 proof equates an expected score-difference norm with Fisher divergence, although Section 2 defines Fisher divergence using the squared norm. The changed warm-start guidance is also unreconciled with Lemma 4.3. These issues leave the reliability of the strengthened interpretation, and thus the net quality improvement, uncertain.
